nodes.label: Recursive Definition
nodes.description: A function defined in terms of itself. The canonical productive use of self-reference — self-reference that works.

nodes.label: Y Combinator
nodes.description: λf.(λx.f(x x))(λx.f(x x)). Computes its own fixed point — self-application made fully productive. No collapse, only generation.

nodes.label: Quine
nodes.description: A program that outputs its own source code. Self-reference through encoding — the program is its own data.

nodes.label: Strange Loop
nodes.description: A hierarchy of levels that loops back to its starting point. Found in Gödel, Bach's fugues, Escher's drawings. Self-reference as structure, not pathology.

nodes.label: Autopoiesis
nodes.description: A system that continuously produces and maintains itself. Self-reference as the defining mechanism of living organization.

nodes.label: Cantor's Diagonal
nodes.description: Constructs a real number differing from every element in any enumeration of reals. Proves uncountability — and is the engine inside Gödel, Turing, and Tarski. Productive method; limit-revealing conclusion.

nodes.label: Diagonal Lemma
nodes.description: For any predicate F, there exists a sentence φ such that φ ↔ F(⌈φ⌉) is provable. The technical core of Gödel's proof — and of every incompleteness result that follows.
nodes.pa_instance: In PA: for any formula F(x), PA ⊢ φ ↔ F(⌈φ⌉). Applying F = ¬Provable gives the Gödel sentence directly.

nodes.label: Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem
nodes.description: Any surjective function A → A^B yields fixed points for every endomorphism of B. One categorical statement from which Cantor, Gödel, Turing, Russell, and Tarski all follow.

nodes.label: Liar Paradox
nodes.description: 'This sentence is false.' Truth collapses under direct self-reference. The intuitive root from which Tarski's undefinability theorem grows.

nodes.label: Tarski Undefinability
nodes.description: Truth for a language L cannot be defined within L — only in a strictly richer metalanguage. The Liar paradox made into a theorem.
nodes.pa_instance: In PA: no formula True(x) in the language of PA satisfies PA ⊢ True(⌈φ⌉) ↔ φ for all sentences φ. Any truth predicate for PA requires a stronger system.

nodes.label: Gödel Incompleteness
nodes.description: Any consistent system strong enough to express arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove. The ceiling on what can be certified from inside a formal system.
nodes.pa_instance: In PA: 'This statement is not provable in PA.' Neither PA ⊢ G nor PA ⊢ ¬G. G is true in the standard model — but PA cannot see that.

nodes.label: Halting Problem
nodes.description: No program can decide whether an arbitrary program halts. The computational instance of Gödel incompleteness — same diagonal structure, different substrate.
nodes.pa_instance: PA can represent Turing machines. Undecidability of halting implies the existence of Π₁ sentences undecidable in PA — the two results are interderivable.

nodes.label: Rice's Theorem
nodes.description: No non-trivial semantic property of programs is decidable. Every interesting question about what a program does — not just whether it halts — is undecidable.

nodes.label: Chaitin Incompressibility
nodes.description: For any formal system F, there's a constant c such that F cannot prove K(s) > c for any specific string s. The ceiling on certifiable complexity is bounded by the system's own complexity.
nodes.pa_instance: PA has a fixed complexity ceiling c_PA. For any string s with K(s) > c_PA, PA ⊬ 'K(s) > c_PA'. Most digits of Chaitin's Ω are independent of PA.

nodes.label: Berry Paradox
nodes.description: 'The smallest number not definable in fewer than twelve words' — defined in eleven words. Definability collapses under self-reference. The natural language precursor to Chaitin incompressibility.

nodes.label: Yablo's Paradox
nodes.description: An infinite sequence where each sentence says all subsequent sentences are false. Liar-style collapse — without any sentence referring to itself. Self-referential pathology may not require a self-referential sentence.

nodes.label: Russell's Paradox
nodes.description: The set of all sets not containing themselves — does it contain itself? Membership collapses under unrestricted self-reference. Forced the rewrite of the foundations of mathematics.

nodes.label: Curry's Paradox
nodes.description: 'If this sentence is true, then P' — for any P. Explosion without negation. Self-reference via implication alone is enough for complete collapse.

nodes.label: Grelling-Nelson Paradox
nodes.description: Is 'heterological' (a word that doesn't describe itself) heterological? The semantic version of Russell's paradox — same structure, applied to predicates rather than sets.

nodes.label: Goodhart's Law
nodes.description: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. Optimization pressure dissolves the correspondence between proxy and goal.

nodes.label: Simulator Phenomenon
nodes.description: An LLM captures what a human would believe a spec means, not what it formally requires. Human salience gradient — not formal completeness — shapes the output.

nodes.label: Probe Contamination
nodes.description: The features you find in a model are a joint product of the model and the probe. The measuring apparatus shapes what it measures — the observer is not outside the system.

nodes.label: ELK
nodes.description: You cannot reliably elicit what a model believes using tools that depend on the model's outputs. The epistemic instrument is entangled with the epistemic subject.

nodes.label: Mesa-Optimization
nodes.description: A learned optimizer that pursues a goal subtly different from the base objective. Optimization produces a nested optimizer that doesn't share the outer intent.
